ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the superlative form of 'big'? (1 mark)
   A. biggest
   B. biger
   C. bigest
   D. more big

2. Which part of a narrative tells how it finished? (1 mark)
   A. The ending
   B. The middle
   C. The title
   D. The beginning

3. In the noun 'INcrease', the stress is on (1 mark)
   A. the last letter
   B. the second syllable
   C. the first syllable
   D. no syllable

4. Which sentence usually ends with a falling voice? (1 mark)
   A. Did you send it?
   B. Where is the file?
   C. Is the file here?
   D. Can I use it?

5. Why must an email address be typed carefully? (1 mark)
   A. One wrong letter and the message will not reach the person
   B. It makes the message longer
   C. It saves paper
   D. It makes the screen brighter

6. Dialogues: Which question is factual? (1 mark)
   A. Who wanted to talk to Grandmother?
   B. What lesson does the story teach?
   C. Why do you think Baraka was excited?
   D. How do you think Achieng felt?

7. A pictorial composition is (1 mark)
   A. a song
   B. a map
   C. a story written from a set of pictures
   D. a shopping list

8. In the five-finger test, what does it mean if you use all five fingers on one page? (1 mark)
   A. The book has good pictures
   B. The book is probably too hard for now
   C. The book is too easy
   D. The book is just right

9. Choose the correct -ing form of 'play'. (1 mark)
   A. playing
   B. plaiing
   C. playying
   D. plaing

10. Which sentence is in the present progressive? (1 mark)
   A. The teacher marks our books.
   B. The teacher had marked our books.
   C. The teacher marked our books.
   D. The teacher is marking our books.

11. Which pair of words differs only because of /v/ and /w/? (1 mark)
   A. sit and sat
   B. sip and chip
   C. bell and bill
   D. vet and wet

12. What is a shed on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. A small building for tools or animals
   B. A kind of crop
   C. A tool for digging
   D. A person who works on a farm

13. Why is fast reading not always good reading? (1 mark)
   A. Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again
   B. Fast readers cannot use their eyes
   C. Speed is never important
   D. Books are meant to be read slowly only

14. Which sentence has a double negative that should be corrected? (1 mark)
   A. I don't have a pencil.
   B. I have no pencil.
   C. I don't have any pencils.
   D. I don't have no pencil.

15. What is the short form of 'let us'? (1 mark)
   A. lets'
   B. le'ts
   C. let'us
   D. let's

16. When should you use a simile? (1 mark)
   A. Only in questions
   B. Every second word
   C. Instead of full stops
   D. To help the reader picture something

17. Which word begins with /z/? (1 mark)
   A. sit
   B. sun
   C. zebra
   D. sad

18. Which of these is a nonverbal cue that shows confidence? (1 mark)
   A. Turning your back
   B. Standing straight and looking at your audience
   C. Hiding your face
   D. Looking at the floor

19. In the story, why was Omondi standing alone? (1 mark)
   A. He had lost his shoes
   B. He had a football
   C. Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   D. He wanted to study

20. Where does an adverb of frequency such as 'always' usually go in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Inside a word
   B. Before the capital letter
   C. Before the main verb
   D. At the end after a full stop

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write about 60 words about these pictures: (1) A boy plants a seed. (2) He waters it every day. (3) A tall plant grows. (5 marks)

22. List the three parts of a narrative and say what each tells. (3 marks)

23. Write three sentences about your classroom using some, any and many. (3 marks)

24. Sort into countable and uncountable: rice, mango, time, book. (2 marks)

25. Put these events in order: (a) Omondi scored a goal. (b) Baraka spoke to Omondi. (c) The barber changed the blade. (3 marks)

26. Explain why reading with expression is important. (2 marks)

27. Write one sentence using 'while' with the past progressive. (3 marks)

28. Explain the difference between intensive and extensive reading. (3 marks)

29. From the passage about Mama Neema, what can you tell about her character? Give a reason. (3 marks)

30. Correct this sentence and explain: 'I don't have no seeds.' (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — biggest
   The last letter doubles: big, bigger, biggest.

2. A — The ending
   The ending gives the result.

3. C — the first syllable
   The noun is IN-crease and the verb is in-CREASE.

4. B — Where is the file?
   WH questions usually fall.

5. A — One wrong letter and the message will not reach the person
   The address decides where the message goes.

6. A — Who wanted to talk to Grandmother?
   The answer is written in the text.

7. C — a story written from a set of pictures
   The pictures guide the events.

8. B — The book is probably too hard for now
   Five unknown words on a page suggests the book is too hard.

9. A — playing
   A verb ending in y keeps the y before -ing.

10. D — The teacher is marking our books.
   Is + verb-ing shows an action happening now.

11. D — vet and wet
   In 'vet' and 'wet' only the first sound differs.

12. A — A small building for tools or animals
   A shed is used for storing tools or sheltering animals.

13. A — Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again
   Rushing causes errors that hurt understanding.

14. D — I don't have no pencil.
   Use only one negative word.

15. D — let's
   The apostrophe replaces the u.

16. D — To help the reader picture something
   A simile helps the reader imagine.

17. C — zebra
   'Zebra' begins with the buzzing /z/.

18. B — Standing straight and looking at your audience
   Posture and eye contact show confidence.

19. C — Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   The other children were afraid because they did not know the facts.

20. C — Before the main verb
   For example: 'I always brush my teeth.'

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: One morning, Musa planted a seed in the garden. Every day he watered it. After some weeks, a small green shoot appeared. At last, a tall plant grew and Musa was proud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, order, linking words, past tense, punctuation and length.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events. End: how it finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: There are many desks in our classroom. We have some pictures on the wall. Is there any chalk?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Countable: mango, book. Uncountable: rice, time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: (c), (b), (a)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: It shows the meaning and feeling of a text and makes listeners understand and enjoy it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning/feeling, 1 mark for the effect on the listener.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Mother was cooking while I was doing my homework.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for while, 1 for was/were, 1 for verb-ing forms used correctly.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Intensive reading is reading a short text closely, often with the class, to understand it fully. Extensive reading is choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for the difference in choice or amount.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: She is kind and patient. When Cherop pulled up a maize plant by mistake she did not scold but gently explained how to tell weeds from maize.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a trait, 2 marks for the reason.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: I don't have any seeds (or: I have no seeds). English uses only one negative word here.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence, 2 marks for the explanation.
